findings.what: Reads as if the election must be made on Form 15620. The IRS says the form is voluntary and a written statement that meets Treas. Reg. 1.83-2 is equally valid, so a reader who already drafted a statement could think it is void. The 30-day deadline, the no-revocation rule and the RSU/option exclusion are all correct.
findings.evidence: Pub 525 (2025), Restricted Property, 'How to make the choice' ('filing a written statement or Form 15620'); Form 15620 instructions, 'Who May File' ('In the alternative, an 83(b) election may be made by filing a written statement') and Privacy Act notice ('its use is voluntary'); https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f15620.pdf
findings.fix: 'It's due within 30 days of the transfer, on Form 15620 or a signed written statement, and can't be revoked without IRS consent.'

findings.what: Gives only 'single' and 'joint'. The IRS table is 'Unmarried Individuals (other than Surviving Spouses)', which includes head of household, so Leo (head of household) uses $90,100 and a $500,000 threshold, but the sheet never says so. Married filing separately ($70,100, $500,000 threshold) is also missing, although the Medicare line does list that status. Every figure that is given is right.
findings.evidence: Rev. Proc. 2025-32, section 4.10 (exemption table: joint $140,200; unmarried $90,100; married filing separately $70,100; phase-out thresholds $1,000,000 / $500,000 / $500,000); IRC 55(d)(1)(B); welcome/checks/work/numbers.py
findings.fix: Write '$90,100 single or head of household, $140,200 joint, $70,100 married filing separately', with the $500,000 threshold shared by single, head of household and separate filers.

findings.where: site/cheat-sheet.md, Cost basis, sentence 1 ('For shares granted after 2013')
findings.what: Narrower than the rule. Form 1099-B instructions bar adding the wage income to basis for compensation arrangements 'granted or acquired after 2013'; Pub 525 says 'options granted on or after January 1, 2014'. A reader whose award was granted earlier but whose shares were acquired in 2026 is still covered by the rule but could read the sentence as excluding them.
findings.evidence: Instructions for Form 1099-B (2026), Specific Instructions, box 1e / basis ('You cannot increase initial basis for income recognized upon the exercise of a compensatory option or the vesting or exercise of other equity-based compensation arrangements granted or acquired after 2013'); Pub 525 (2025), Nonstatutory Stock Options, 'Sale of the stock'
findings.fix: 'For stock granted or acquired after 2013, Form 1099-B can't include what was taxed as wages...'

findings.where: site/cheat-sheet.md, ESPP and ISO holding periods, 'ESPP, qualifying' bullet
findings.what: 'The lesser of the actual gain and the grant-date discount' gives a negative number if the shares are sold at a loss. Pub 525 says a loss means no ordinary income. (The ISO bullet's 'capped at the gain' has the same gap but is clearer.) The 15 percent arithmetic is right: with a 15% plan the grant-date discount is 15% of the grant-date value, and my rerun of Pub 525 Examples 10 and 11 matches.
findings.evidence: Pub 525 (2025), Statutory Stock Options, 'Option granted at a discount' and Examples 10 and 11; welcome/checks/work/numbers.py
findings.fix: Add 'or zero if you sold at a loss' to both bullets.

findings.where: site/cheat-sheet.md, Dates for 2026 returns, rows 'February 1, 2027' (3921/3922) and 'February 16, 2027' (1099-B)
findings.what: These two dates are derived, not quoted. The IRS has not yet published the 2026 General Instructions for Certain Information Returns. The derivation is sound (Jan 31, 2027 is a Sunday so Monday Feb 1; Feb 15, 2027 is Washington's Birthday so Tuesday Feb 16, and the 2025 instructions show the same pattern: Feb 2 and Feb 17, 2026), and the W-2 date of Feb 1, 2027 is stated outright in the 2026 W-2 instructions. Re-check when the 2026 instructions are posted.
findings.evidence: IRC 6039(b) (Jan 31); IRC 7503; 5 U.S.C. 6103 (third Monday in February); 26 CFR 1.6045-1(k)(2) (Feb 15); General Instructions for Certain Information Returns (2025), part M; General Instructions for Forms W-2 and W-3 (2026); welcome/checks/work/numbers.py
findings.fix: Keep the dates; add the 2026 General Instructions for Certain Information Returns to Sources once published, as part of the January rollover re-check the file header already calls for.
